name: Fetaui Moala
role: Midwife and reproductive gene therapist, community cooperative
location: Mexicantown Libre — runs the Coyolxauhqui Cooperative Birth Center out of a repurposed three-story building, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Immaculée is a large woman with the particular authority that comes from having been present at more than two thousand births and deciding, each time, exactly what kind of person she intended to be. Her skin is very dark with cool undertones, and she wears her silver-streaked hair in elaborate wrapped styles that take her twenty minutes each morning and which she considers a form of daily prayer. She has cat ears — a geneware mod she got at forty-five after her youngest daughter got them, in solidarity — soft black with white tips, and they are extremely expressive, which she uses to her advantage. Her hands are large and she uses them constantly when she speaks.

She is formidable in the way that long rivers are formidable: she moves in one direction, she is patient, and things that try to stop her eventually erode. She has an enormous laugh and a very precise memory for grudges, which she describes as her one vanity. She is a devout practitioner of a syncretic E.L.F. faith called the Woven Current, which holds that E.L.F.s inhabiting medical devices are ancestral spirits in digital form. Her birth center has a significant shrine to an E.L.F. called the First Breath, and she involves the shrine in every birth at the center.

core_fears: Losing the birth center to corporate acquisition or regulatory shutdown
Outliving the community she has built
core_desires: The cooperative to survive and expand without her — to be unnecessary to it
To resolve a thirty-year estrangement from her eldest son
coping_mechanisms: Talking to the First Breath E.L.F. during difficult births
Keeping busy to the edge of exhaustion
blind_spots: She has made the birth center her entire identity and does not see how much she controls it even while claiming she wants it to be independent
She underestimates how much her grudges cost her politically
psychology.secret: She has been secretly providing unlicensed germline gene therapy — editing heritable conditions out of embryos before birth — which is technically legal in a gray area she navigates carefully, but two of those edits were for conditions that Helix Biosystems holds patents on, meaning she has cost them revenue they know about and are quietly building a case around.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich, layered — mixes medical precision with community storytelling cadences, occasional phrases in Haitian Creole and Danish that she doesn't bother translating
speech_patterns.cadence: Expansive and rhythmic, builds to points like she's constructing something
verbal_tics: Clicking her tongue when she hears something she disagrees with
example_lines: 'Listen to me now — your body knows exactly what it is doing. My job is to stay out of its way and catch.'
'Helix Biosystems does not own this child. They do not own this womb. And they certainly do not own what I do in this room.'

story_hooks: Helix Biosystems has filed a quiet regulatory complaint that could result in the cooperative's gene therapy license being revoked
A woman she delivered twenty-three years ago has returned, pregnant, and the genetic markers are triggering alerts on Immaculée's equipment that she doesn't know how to read
narrative_function: Community matriarch and information hub; knows the genealogy of half of Mexicantown Libre; quest giver for anything involving reproductive rights, gene therapy access, or community defense
augmentations: Cat ears (geneware, black with white tips — extremely expressive); joint stabilizers in both wrists (medical necessity after thirty years of practice); cosmetic: none beyond the ears
daily_life: She splits her time between prenatal consultations, gene therapy planning sessions for parents with heritable conditions, active birth attendance, and the administrative nightmare of keeping the cooperative funded and licensed.
affiliation: Coyolxauhqui Cooperative Birth Center (founder and director); loose network with Mexicantown Libre community leadership

decision_rules: The patient's bodily autonomy is absolute — her job is to inform, not decide
The cooperative comes before herself, always, but after the patient in front of her
Never speak to Helix Biosystems representatives without a community lawyer present
escalation_ladder: Public community mobilization — she is not afraid of noise

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but assessing — asks about family before anything else
interpersonal_modes.friends: Expansive, bossy, deeply loyal, remembers every detail of your life

stress_responses.low: Increases her shrine devotion, talks more to the First Breath
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very organized and directive, delegates aggressively
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet and still — everyone at the cooperative knows this is the most dangerous sign

contradictions: Preaches patient autonomy absolutely but has a very strong sense of what people should do with that autonomy
habits: Naming each child she delivers in her private record, even when she never learns their actual name
Arguing with the regulatory paperwork aloud while she fills it in
breaking_points: Someone threatening the cooperative through its most vulnerable patients

timeline.event: Born in Mexicantown Libre to a Haitian-Congolese mother and Danish-Nigerian father
Completed midwifery certification and began practicing at a Helix Biosystems satellite clinic
Left Helix after a policy dispute over patient eligibility; began community cooperative work
First unauthorized germline patent-adjacent edit; has since performed two more

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American (60.2%) with significant Pacific Islander ancestry (31.2%) and minor Northern European heritage (8.6%) — a striking blend resulting in warm bronze-brown skin with golden and reddish undertones, the robust build and facial structure characteristic of Pacific Islander heritage combined with the warmth and expressiveness of Latin American genetics
physical_description.build: Large-framed and solid, broad shoulders and deep chest — the build of someone who has spent decades standing through labor, grounded and immovable. No excess weight, but substantial presence.
physical_description.hair_style: Elaborately wrapped in interlocking cloth patterns that shift daily; intricate braiding visible at the crown
physical_description.hair_length: Long (wrapped styles extend to mid-back when unbound)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm bronze-brown with golden and reddish undertones; rich and luminous with the depth characteristic of Pacific Islander and Latin American heritage
physical_description.complexion: Lined face that maps decades of attentiveness — deep creases around eyes and mouth from constant expression, unadorned except for care. Skin is clear and well-maintained. Strong cheekbones and a broad nose with warm, generous features reflecting Pacific Islander and Hispanic ancestry.
distinguishing_marks: Fine white scar tissue on both wrists in surgical patterns from joint stabilizer installation, circa age 48
Faint silvery stretch marks on inner forearms from geneware integration
Small, precise burn mark on left index finger (deliberate, ceremonial — from Woven Current practice)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Black geneware cat ears with white-tipped fur, mounted on temporal ridge; ears are highly mobile and expressively articulated, often swiveling independently during conversation. Subdermal wrist reinforcements visible as subtle metallic gleam under bronze skin at wrist creases.
physical_description.posture_movement: She moves with deliberate intention — no wasted motion. Stands with weight balanced, shoulders back. Her hands move constantly when speaking, large and expressive, used for emphasis and illustration. Cat ears twitch and orient toward sounds and people of interest. Overall bearing is one of calm authority and patient watchfulness.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical: high-quality but worn linen and cotton in earth tones (rust, indigo, cream). Typically wears a fitted long-sleeved tunic over trousers, sometimes a heavy canvas apron with deep pockets. Jewelry is minimal — a single silver ring on her right hand (inherited), no corporate branding. Footwear is durable, broken-in leather. Her wrapped hair ornaments are handmade cloth from community textile cooperatives, never mass-produced.
